question: Assume today is 2026-09-06. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of recreation visits to Yellowstone National Park in September 2026, as it will be reported in the National Park Service's official monthly visitation statistics.

target.what: Recreation visits to Yellowstone National Park as reported in the National Park Service's official monthly visitation statistics. A recreation visit is one person entering the park for recreational purposes; the same person entering multiple times on separate occasions counts as multiple visits.
target.publisher: National Park Service (NPS), typically via the Visitor Use Statistics program / Integrated Resource Management Applications (IRMA) and the NPS monthly visitation report.
target.cadence: Monthly, usually published with a lag of several weeks to a few months after the month ends.
target.caveats: The target period is future relative to the 2026-09-06 cutoff. The estimate must rely on historical seasonal patterns, recent 2026 monthly data (through July or August 2026 if published), and any available signals for September 2026. The NPS definition of a recreation visit excludes non-recreation e

candidates.perspective: NPS historical monthly visitation statistics for Yellowstone National Park
candidates.hypothesis: September recreation visits in recent years (2015–2025) show a stable seasonal pattern and trend. The 2026 September value can be estimated by applying the historical September share of annual visits or by extrapolating the recent September trend, adjusted for any known shocks (e.g., 2022 flood closure).
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly recreation visit counts for Yellowstone for September 2015–2025, and annual totals for the same years. Also, the most recent 2026 monthly counts (January–August 2026) if published before 2026-09-06. Minimum evidence: September counts for at least the last 5 years and the 2026 year-to-date total.
search_hints: Yellowstone National Park monthly visitation statistics September 2025
NPS Yellowstone recreation visits by month 2020-2025

candidates.perspective: National Park Service overall visitation and Yellowstone's share
candidates.hypothesis: Yellowstone's September recreation visits are a roughly stable share of total NPS September recreation visits or of visitation to a comparable set of large western parks. If NPS-wide September 2026 data or a nowcast is available, Yellowstone's share can be applied.
candidates.data_to_find: NPS-wide monthly recreation visits for September 2015–2025 and any preliminary September 2026 NPS-wide figures. Also, September visitation for comparable parks (Grand Teton, Glacier, Yosemite) to check relative patterns. Minimum evidence: NPS-wide September totals and Yellowstone's share in recent Septembers.
search_hints: National Park Service monthly visitation report September 2025
Yellowstone share of NPS visitation September

candidates.perspective: Entrance station counts and vehicle occupancy
candidates.hypothesis: Recreation visits can be estimated from the number of vehicles entering Yellowstone in September multiplied by average persons per vehicle, plus pedestrian/bicycle entries. Entrance counts may be available from park traffic counters or gateway community data.
candidates.data_to_find: September vehicle entry counts at Yellowstone's five entrances (or total) for recent years, and average occupancy rates (persons per vehicle) from NPS surveys or traffic studies. Minimum evidence: at least one recent September with both vehicle counts and occupancy estimates.
search_hints: Yellowstone average persons per vehicle visitation

candidates.perspective: Accommodation occupancy and campground use in Yellowstone and gateway communities
candidates.hypothesis: Overnight stays in the park and surrounding areas are a major component of visits. September occupancy rates and room/campsite capacity can be used to estimate overnight visits, which can be combined with day-use estimates.
candidates.data_to_find: September occupancy rates for Yellowstone lodges and campgrounds (e.g., Xanterra, Delaware North) for recent years, total room/campsite capacity, and average length of stay. Also, gateway community hotel occupancy data for September. Minimum evidence: September occupancy and capacity for at least one recent year.

candidates.hypothesis: September visitation is sensitive to road closures, wildfires, weather events, and the timing of Labor Day. In 2026, any known closures or major events (e.g., road construction) could shift visitation. The 2022 flood caused a dramatic drop; other years had minor disruptions.
candidates.data_to_find: Yellowstone road closure announcements, wildfire reports, and weather summaries for September 2026 (if available before cutoff) or historical September disruptions. Also, the date of Labor Day 2026 (September 7) and its effect on the month's distribution. Minimum evidence: any known major closures or events affecting September 2026.

candidates.perspective: Published forecasts or nowcasts for Yellowstone 2026 visitation
candidates.hypothesis: Tourism forecasts, park concessionaire projections, or economic outlooks for the Yellowstone region may provide a September 2026 visitation estimate or a growth rate that can be applied to historical September data.
candidates.data_to_find: Any 2026 visitation forecast for Yellowstone or Wyoming/Montana tourism, including from NPS, University of Montana, or local tourism boards. Minimum evidence: a forecast for 2026 annual or monthly visitation with a stated methodology.

candidates.hypothesis: September visitation can be modeled as a function of the number of days, weekends, and Labor Day timing. Historical September data can yield a base rate per day, which can be adjusted for the 2026 calendar (e.g., Labor Day on September 7).
candidates.data_to_find: Daily or weekly visitation data for Yellowstone in September for recent years, or monthly totals with day counts. Minimum evidence: September monthly totals and the number of weekend days/Labor Day date for each year.
search_hints: Yellowstone visitation by day of week

candidates.perspective: Search interest and social media activity as a leading indicator
candidates.hypothesis: Google Trends search volume for 'Yellowstone National Park' or related terms in the weeks before and during September 2026 may correlate with actual visitation. A historical correlation can be used to nowcast September visits.
candidates.data_to_find: Google Trends data for 'Yellowstone' or 'Yellowstone National Park' for September 2015–2025 and available 2026 data, along with corresponding monthly visitation. Minimum evidence: a consistent correlation between search interest and visitation in September.

assessment.note: These four daily parkwide vehicle-entry counts form a coherent Labor Day weekend 2021 series (Fri-Mon). They are internally consistent with the entrance-level counts p28-p32 and p34 for the same weekend, and they are the only kept daily physical-flow observations for early September. They are not independent of the entrance-level points because the parkwide totals are sums of the entrance counts.

These are the 2019 comparison days for the same Labor Day weekend window. They are used only as a historical analogue for the calendar structure of early September, not as a direct level for 2026. They corroborate the seasonal shape seen in p20-p23.

Entrance-level vehicle entries for Friday and Saturday of Labor Day weekend 2021. They sum approximately to the parkwide totals p20 and p21, so they are not independent measurements; they are useful for checking entrance shares and for any route that needs a specific entrance mix.

The 21% parkwide increase for Labor Day weekend 2021 over 2019 is consistent with the ratio of p20-p23 to p24-p27. It is a derived summary of the same underlying counts, not an independent observation.

Google search lead over Grand Canyon for July 2025-June 2026 is a demand/attention signal, not a visit count. It can only support a qualitative or wide-bounded adjustment; it does not provide a September 2026 level or a reliable conversion to recreation visits.

params.formula: ((p20 + p21 + p22 + p23) / 4) * k_days_target * a1 * a2

methods.rationale: Physical-flow route: average daily parkwide vehicle entries from the 2021 Labor Day weekend (p20-p23) are scaled by a September 2026 change factor (a2) and multiplied by days in September (k_days_target) and persons per vehicle (a1). This yields recreation visits for September 2026. Shared dependencies: a1 and a2 are both uncertain and multiply the same base; the 2021 weekend is a high-traffic anchor, so a2 must capture the post-holiday weekday decline and any 2026-specific shocks. Failure modes: if 2026 September has a major closure or if average occupancy differs substantially from the assumed range, the estimate will be biased. The route does not use any 2026 monthly data because none are kept.

assumptions.name: Persons per vehicle factor for Yellowstone September recreation visits
assumptions.rationale: NPS and park studies commonly report average vehicle occupancy in the range of about 2.0 to 3.2 for western national parks, with family and group travel in September. The kept vehicle-entry points do not supply this factor, so it must be assumed. The range is deliberately wide to reflect uncertainty across entrance mix and trip type.
assumptions.applies_when: Used to convert parkwide vehicle entries to recreation visits for a September period at Yellowstone, assuming the same average occupancy applies to all entrances and days.
assumptions.falsified_by: A Yellowstone-specific persons-per-vehicle study or NPS occupancy count showing average occupancy outside 2.0-3.2 for September.

assumptions.name: September 2026 parkwide vehicle entries relative to Labor Day weekend 2021 daily average
assumptions.rationale: The kept daily vehicle-entry points are for Labor Day weekend 2021, which was a high-visitation period. September 2026 is a future month with unknown conditions. The ratio is centered slightly below 1 because early September includes post-Labor Day weekdays with lower traffic, but the range is wide to cover weather, road closures, and demand shifts. This is a change factor, not a target level.
assumptions.applies_when: Used to scale the average daily vehicle entries from the 2021 Labor Day weekend to an average September 2026 day, before multiplying by days in September and persons per vehicle.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence of a major 2026 September disruption (wildfire, road closure, flood) or a strong 2026 visitation trend that puts the ratio outside 0.55-1.30.

assessment.note: These four daily parkwide vehicle-entry counts for the 2021 Labor Day weekend are internally consistent and show the expected holiday pattern (Saturday/Sunday peak, Monday decline). They are the only kept direct physical-flow observations for early September, but they cover a single holiday weekend in 2021, not a full month, and not 2026.

These four daily parkwide vehicle-entry counts for the 2019 Labor Day weekend are the comparison-year counterpart to p20–p23. They are consistent with the 2021 series and support the 21% weekend-over-weekend increase reported in p33.

The 2019 and 2021 daily counts and the reported 21% parkwide increase are mutually consistent. They share the same NPS source and measurement basis, so they are not independent of one another, but they jointly establish a usable early-September vehicle-entry level and year-over-year change for a pre-2026 analogue.

Entrance-level counts for Friday and Saturday of the 2021 Labor Day weekend sum approximately to the parkwide totals in p20 and p21, confirming internal consistency of the entrance decomposition. They are useful for understanding entrance mix but do not add independent information about the September 2026 level.

Google search lead over Grand Canyon is a demand-attention signal, not a visitation count. It has no established conversion to Yellowstone September recreation visits and covers a 12-month window ending June 2026, so it can only serve as weak qualitative context, not a numerical input.

The September 2024 recreation-visit total of 852,435 and its 2.2% drop from August 2024 provide a recent full-month September level and a seasonal August-to-September ratio. This is the single most relevant kept observation for anchoring a September 2026 estimate, though it is from 2024 and must be transferred forward.

assumptions.name: September 2026 vehicle entries relative to the 2021 Labor Day weekend daily average

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.

ablation.rule: exclude points from own_history directions and points whose name contains a target entity anchor and whose name or unit shares a stem with the target unit (triangulate/agent/ablation.py)
residual_risks: Own values named by an alias or abbreviation, or with no entity in the point name, are not excluded.

The rule over-excludes on purpose: any point naming the target entity together with the target quantity (for example a survey of the target's visitors) is excluded, even when it is not a value of the target itself.
The model's own memory of the target's history is not removed: it can still shape the plan, the judge's choices and assumption values.
The searcher and the extractor still see pages that contain own values; only the judge's table is filtered.
